title: NASA releases 3D stereo anaglyph of comet 67P
excerpt: The image features the nucleus of Churyumov-Gerasimenko as captured by the Rosetta spacecraft in 2015.
bodyHtml:
NASA published a 3D stereo anaglyph of the comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko, also known as Comet 67P. The image displays the jagged and double-lobed nucleus of the comet. The larger lobe is around 4 kilometers in diameter, joined to a smaller, 2.5 kilometer diameter lobe by a narrow neck.

The stereo anaglyph was created by combining two images from the Rosetta spacecraft's narrow angle OSIRIS camera taken on July 25, 2015 from a distance of 184 kilometers. Numerous jets are emanating from the small solar system world's active surface near its closest approach to the Sun.

Rosetta's mission to the comet ended in September 2016 when the spacecraft was commanded to a controlled impact with the comet's surface. A catalog of nearly 1400 stereo anaglyphs created from Rosetta image data is available on the website. The stereo anaglyph was created by Philippe Lamy and The Team.
